newsitem.title: USA: Dollar ends lower in U.S. as Dow sheds 100 points.
newsitem.headline: Dollar ends lower in U.S. as Dow sheds 100 points.

text.p: The dollar pared early gains to end lower in the U.S. against most European currencies, dragged down by a sharp retreat in U.S. stocks for a second consecutive session.
The dollar rose in European and early U.S. trade, bolstered by optimism that ongoing negotiations in Dublin over a proposed European monetary pact will end in the U.S. unit's favor.

Currency analysts said market-makers on Thursday bought dollars in order to benefit from the likelihood of a relatively weak or ineffective stability pact, which would put the mark under pressure against the dollar and other European currencies.

"I think there have been enough comments to influence the sentiment that not a great amount will be achieved. The market has become pessimistic," said David Durrant, senior currency strategist at consulting firm I.D.E.A.
Molding market opinion were vocal European negotiators in Dublin who expressed doubt over the stability pact's chances.
Several officials warned against premature optimism.
"According to our latest information, one should be careful with such expectations," said Austrian Chancellor Franz Vranitzky.
The talks precede the EU summit starting on Friday which have grabbed the currency market's focus and spurred much speculation over the liklihood of European monetary union.

"I think the market was so optimistic last week with everyone saying monetary union was definately going to happen and this week the sentiment is not so great," Greg Perman, Credit Commerciale de France foreign exchange manager, said.
The dollar also received support from European Monetary Institute president Alexandre Lamfalussy who said the dollar was undervalued against European currencies.
An unexpected drop of 0.4 percent in U.S. November retail sales against a consensus forecast for a 0.3 percent gain, also helped fuel the dollar's rise along with other U.S. asset markets.

But by late trade, U.S. Treasuries had erased almost all of their gains and the Dow Jones closed off almost 100 points after an initial 30 point gain. The dollar followed suit and pared its gains versus most European currencies.
The dollar closed at 1.5405/15 marks compared to 1.5445/50 marks at Thursday's open. The dollar also pared gains against the yen, ending unchanged at 113.15/20 yen.

The dollar fell sharply in Asian trade against the yen, but a bout of Australian dollar buying and yen selling brought the slide to a halt. Heavy buying by a U.S. money fund also aided the dollar's recovery versus the yen, dealers said.
The market was little moved by tame November U.S. consumer price data. The CPI index rose 0.3 percent, as expected.

In other trading, the dollar fell to 1.3105/15 Swiss francs from 1.3155/65 at Wednesday's open and to Canadian $1.3585/90 from C$1.3591/96. Sterling rose to $1.6565/75 from $1.6523/33. The Australian dollar closed down at $0.7923/28 from $0.7930/35 at the open.
